Ubayy b. Ka'b swore that Lailat-ul-Qadr is in Ramadan, on the twenty-seventh night, and that the sun rises next morning bright without rays.
Seeing companions' dreams agree, the Prophet said to seek Lailat-ul-Qadr in the last seven or ten nights of Ramadan, the odd ones, and said he was shown it but forgot.
Seeking Lailat-ul-Qadr in i'tikaf, the Prophet was told it lay in the last ten odd nights and saw himself prostrating in water and clay, which rain left on his forehead.
Seek Lailat-ul-Qadr in the last ten nights; Ubayy b. Ka'b swore it is the twenty-seventh, with a rayless sunrise, and the Prophet mentioned a moon like a piece of plate.
